title: Slab Specter: heap compactor trigger + KV index heal to stop intermittent GPU OOMs
creator: Priya Nair
description: Multiple customers (hosted and dedicated) have escalated intermittent GPU OOMs during medium-length chat sessions. Investigation shows correlated memory fragmentation in the runtime slab allocator and a subtle KV index stale-pointer condition that prevents tombstone/evicted entries from freeing arena memory. The combined effect causes memory blowups under bursty multi-tenant traffic and long-lived sessions. This ticket contains the runtime patch, validation plan, and rollout steps to stop OOM cascades and repair affected nodes.
reproduction_steps: 1) Replay customer request trace: 30-60s sequences with alternating short prompts (8-64 tokens) and sporadic 2-3k token responses
2) Use stress harness with mixed session affinity across 48 concurrent sessions and aggressive KV churn (inserts+evicts) to emulate tombstone accumulation
3) Observe slab arena fragmentation growth in /metrics/runtime/arena_fragmentation and concurrent stalled evict counts in /metrics/kv/evict_stalled
4) Trigger until OOM in a 4-GPU node (p4d-like) to validate reproduction locally
root_cause_summary: A race between KV eviction path and the slab allocator's lazy free path allowed tombstoned index entries to retain lightweight handles which kept arena pages pinned. The slab compactor is only triggered at high watermarks; under certain churn patterns fragmentation grows without crossing the threshold. The index stale-pointer bug prevented periodic heal sweeps from completing, leaving a growing set of non-reclaimable allocations that ultimately exhaust GPU memory and cause OOMs.
proposed_fix_summary: 1) Lower slab compactor trigger thresholds and add an adaptive compaction heuristic based on fragmentation delta rather than absolute watermark. 2) Fix KV refcount drift in evict path (off-by-one under concurrent race). 3) Add a background tombstone reconciliation pass that unpins stale handles and coalesces freed ranges. 4) Add a startup 'KV index heal' operation for nodes with corrupted index segments to rebuild safe pointers before accepting traffic.
mitigation_steps_taken: 1) Emergency throttle on affected host pools (hosted-us-west-2) to reduce churn while we validate patches
2) Manual session eviction for top offending tenants (tracked in incident INC-2026-0347) to temporarily free KV pressure
3) Enabled temporary aggressive GC on dedicated nodes for high-SLA customers until patch can be rolled out
testing_and_validation: Unit tests added for refcount paths and compactor heuristic (runtime/tests/allocator_test.cc)
Integration harness: reproducer-runner job (ci/stress/repro-oom) to validate OOM does not occur in 2h continuous churn
Canary: deploy to two canary hosts in hosted-us-east-1 with synthetic traffic mirroring customer traces
rollout_plan: Phase 1: apply patch to canary hosts (2 nodes) and monitor 24h. Phase 2: expand to 20% of hosted pool + dedicated canary customers. Phase 3: global rollout with surge window and on-call coverage. If regressions are observed, automatic rollback policy to previous runtime image within 15 minutes.
